subject: Hosted quickstart access and rate-limit check — BrightHarbor POC
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@blueharbor.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted quickstart access and rate-limit check — BrightHarbor POC

Hi Alice — thanks again for the demo earlier. Really appreciated the clarity on the two main workflows you want to validate (customer support summarization + realtime search over docs). Quick recap and a few questions so we can scope the hosted pilot: 

- Goal: 2-week hosted POC to validate latency and per-call cost across typical query sizes (~120–800 tokens).
- Success criteria: median token latency < 250ms for short prompts, 95th < 800ms for longer flows; throughput ~30 concurrent users; cost estimate within the budget band we discussed.

Open items we need from your side:
1) Confirm whether any requests will include customer PII or regulated data (HIPAA/FinServ). This affects whether we recommend Dedicated or Private.
2) Can you share an expected traffic window (RPS) per endpoint and typical prompt length distributions? Even rough numbers are fine.
3) Who handles procurement? I cc'd procurement email earlier — if you prefer, we can draft a short SOW/PO template.

Next steps on our side: we can provision a hosted trial project with a staging API key and two pre-configured endpoints (conversational & embeddings). The staging endpoints are rate-limited by default to 60 rps and a 2,000-token context for the trial; we can adjust if you need higher throughput. Attached is a quickstart checklist and our ratecard snapshot for the POC.

Available times for a 20-min follow-up to finalize pilot params: Mon/Tue 11–2 PT or Wed 8–11 PT. Say the word and I'll send calendar invites.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you started.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@blueharbor.ai>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted quickstart access and rate-limit check — BrightHarbor POC

Hi Mateo — thanks for the recap and the materials. Quick answers below: 

1) Data classification: initial test data will be anonymized transcripts (no direct PII). Production could include PII later; we'll flag that when we get closer to go-live.
2) Traffic: our first test group is ~25 concurrent agents. Typical user flows: 1–3 short queries (~80–150 tokens) per minute and occasional long context queries (~600 tokens) when agents pull case history. So average RPS estimate ~1.2, burst to 50–60 during peak.
3) Procurement: procurement@blueharbor.ai is the contact; PO lead is Tom (cc'd). They prefer a 30-day net invoice, but we'll confirm.

Questions for you before we accept the trial: 
- Can the hosted staging endpoints be restricted to IP ranges (we can provide a static IP block)?
- You mentioned rate limits of 60 rps for the trial — can you confirm how that translates to token budgets and concurrent request handling? We want to ensure the long-context calls won't be throttled mid-response.

If you can answer those two items, we'll greenlight the 2-week pilot. Happy to take the short call tomorrow morning (9:00 PT) if that helps.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Product Ops | BlueHarbor
alice.chen@blueharbor.ai
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@blueharbor.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted quickstart access and rate-limit check — BrightHarbor POC

Hi Alice — great, thanks for the details and the quick turnaround. Answers below — copying Soojin from our infra team for the IP + throttling nuance.

IP restrictions: yes — for the hosted trial we can lock the staging API key to an allowlist of up to 10 CIDR entries. If you provide the range(s) we will apply them before issuing keys. For production hosted customers we offer more advanced VPC peering and private networking patterns, but for the 2-week POC the CIDR allowlist is usually sufficient.

Rate limits and token budgets: our trial default is 60 requests/sec per project. That is enforced at the request-level (not token-level), but the runtime includes per-request token ceilings (2,000 tokens for the staging env). Practically this means: 
- Short prompts (<=200 tokens) are handled with sub-250ms median for the models we suggested.
- Long-context calls (500–800 tokens) will queue briefly under a sustained burst; we use adaptive batching so single long responses shouldn't be truncated mid-response — they may incur added latency if the system is busy.

If you expect sustained bursts where >30% of calls are long-context concurrently, we recommend asking for a temporary rate uplift for the pilot (we can increase to 120 rps and raise token limit to 4,000 for the trial window). That requires a brief ops approval but we can usually grant it same-day.

Pilot provisioning plan (what I'll do after you confirm):
1) Create project 'BrightHarbor-POC' and stage keys locked to your CIDRs.
2) Provision two endpoints: bh-conv (chat) and bh-embed (vector).
3) Apply default trial quotas (60 rps / 2k tokens) unless you request uplift.
4) Send test data upload instructions for embeddings and a short postman collection for smoke tests.

Soojin — can you confirm whether a same-day uplift to 120 rps + 4k token cap is feasible for a 2-week window if BrightHarbor requests it? Also flag any operational notes (sticky IP, monitoring hooks).

Thanks — if tomorrow 9:00 PT works I'll send a calendar invite.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick operational confirmation from infra: we can approve a one-time trial uplift to 120 rps and 4,000 token context for a two-week window. Notes: 

- Please provide the list of CIDR blocks for API key allowlist before keys are issued.
- We will enable a shorter metrics retention (7 days) for the POC by default; if you need longer retention we can enable it as an add-on.
- Monitoring: we'll send a Grafana link with token/latency dashboards and a webhook you can hit for error alerts.
- Sticky IPs: staging keys will honor the allowlisted CIDRs; if you require a single static egress IP we can discuss Dedicated or Private options later.

Mateo — I'll queue the uplift and prepare the staging project once we have the CIDRs and a PO/approval from procurement for the pilot credits.

Alice/Tom — if you confirm the CIDRs and procurement timeline (PO by end of next week?), I'll provision the keys same day we get those items.
